method: Lusk 2010 abstract read on the Penn State research portal; Lopez 2021, Singer 2024, ACSM 2009 and Helms 2016 as in content/evidence/r031.json (abstracts read 2026-11-28). Owner policy from r031: the video names each machine and how to use it, then sets, reps, rest and progression; studies only in the caption.

claims.claim: In the lat pull-down, a pronated (palms forward) grip gave more latissimus dorsi activity than a supinated grip, whatever the grip width.
claims.source_title: Grip width and forearm orientation effects on muscle activity during the lat pull-down
claims.authors: Lusk SJ, Hale BD, Russell DM
claims.finding: Pronated grip elicited greater LD activity than supinated (p < 0.05); anterior pull-down with pronated grip recommended irrespective of grip width. Measured activity, not growth.

claims.claim: Beginners: 3 sets of 8-12 repetitions; increase the load by about 2-10% when the top of the range is exceeded.
claims.source_title: Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
claims.finding: Novice: 1-3 sets of 8-12 repetitions; 2-10% load increase when 1-2 reps over the target can be done on two consecutive sessions.

claims.claim: Rest about 90-120 s between sets: rest longer than 60 s gave a small hypertrophy benefit, with no clear difference beyond about 90 s.
claims.source_title: Give it a rest: a systematic review with Bayesian meta-analysis on the effect of inter-set rest interval duration on muscle hypertrophy
claims.authors: Singer A, Wolf M, Generoso L, et al., Schoenfeld BJ
claims.finding: Small hypertrophic benefit for inter-set rest >60 s; no appreciable difference beyond 90 s (abstract read on frontiersin.org).

claims.claim: Pick a load that leaves about 2-3 repetitions in reserve (practical guidance, caption only).
claims.source_title: Application of the Repetitions in Reserve-Based Rating of Perceived Exertion Scale for Resistance Training
claims.authors: Helms ER, Cronin J, Storey A, Zourdos MC
claims.finding: RIR-based scale for choosing and adjusting load.

claims.claim: Muscle growth was similar across low, moderate and high loads; strength rose more with moderate and high loads, so 8-12 reps is a practical middle (caption only).
claims.source_title: Resistance Training Load Effects on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gain: Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis
claims.authors: Lopez P, Radaelli R, Taaffe DR, Newton RU, Galvão DA, Trajano GS, Teodoro JL, Kraemer WJ, Häkkinen K, Pinto RS
claims.study_type: Systematic review and network meta-analysis: 28 studies, 747 healthy adults
claims.finding: No differences in hypertrophy between loads (low >15RM, moderate 9-15RM, high <=8RM); strength gains superior for high and moderate vs low load.
